`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90` — `group.users.delete(user_id)` resolves the Integer via `find`, so removing a non-member (or stale double-click) raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` → 500 instead of the JSON contract; HEAD~2 succeeded silently and had a spec for it that this diff deleted.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90` — asymmetric lifecycle: adds go through `group.add(user)` but removals bypass `Group#remove`, deleting join rows with `delete_all` semantics — GroupUser callbacks / cached `user_count` are skipped on removal only, leaving `BasicGroupSerializer`'s `user_count` stale in the admin group list.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:77,92` — `group.save` is dead code in both `add_members` and `remove_member`: the group has no dirty attributes, so it always returns true and the `render_json_error` branch is unreachable.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73` — re-adding an existing member is an unguarded check-then-insert: either `RecordNotUnique` (500) with a unique index, or duplicate memberships without one. Made easy to hit because the username input is never cleared.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71` — no transaction around the add loop; a mid-loop failure leaves a partially applied batch and the handler is not idempotent.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38` — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is unconditional, so any partial PUT omitting `visible` silently makes the group invisible; every other field on the action is presence-guarded.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:25,38` — `params[:visible] == "true"` string-compares a boolean; a JSON client sending real `true` silently gets `visible = false`.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22` — `create` accepts only `name`/`visible`, but `Group#asJSON` always sends `alias_level`; on create it is silently dropped, requiring a second round-trip. Create and update accept divergent field sets for the same resource.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34` — `update` now silently *ignores* `usernames`: `PUT /admin/groups/:id` with `group[usernames]` (full member-list replace at HEAD~2) returns `success_json` while making no membership change. Silent semantics break for non-UI/API callers.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22` + `admin/templates/group.hbs:12` — creating a group with an initial member set in one step is gone (member UI gated behind `{{#if id}}`); the spec covering it was deleted.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:52,69,88` — the `automatic` guard is hand-rolled in three actions with no `before_filter` (and `update` deliberately omits it); new actions default to unguarded, and the invariant is enforced only in the controller, not the model.

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22` — `limit` is attacker-controlled and uncapped on a publicly reachable endpoint: `GET /groups/trust_level_0/members.json?limit=99999999` serializes the entire user base — bulk enumeration + resource exhaustion. HEAD~2 had a 200 ceiling for automatic groups; this diff removed the ceiling while adding the knob. Needs `[limit, 200].min`.

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23` — `offset = params[:offset].to_i` unvalidated → `OFFSET -1` is a Postgres `StatementInvalid` → unhandled 500. The clamp exists only client-side in `models/group.js:23`.

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22` — the public endpoint now paginates *all* groups at default 50 (HEAD~2: unpaginated for non-automatic, 200 for automatic), but `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` gained no paging controls — the public group members page is silently truncated at 50 with no way to page. It also discards the HEAD~2 TODO's intent ("fix the root cause") by generalizing the truncation.

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28` — response shape changed from a bare JSON array to `{members:, meta:}`: an unversioned breaking change to a public endpoint, with no compat shim and no spec (`spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` does not exist).

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25` — `total = group.users.count` runs a COUNT per page fetch, duplicating the existing `user_count` column the serializer already exposes; the client overwrites the serializer value with `meta.total`, so which wins depends on load order.

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26` — OFFSET pagination with `ORDER BY username_lower` over the join degrades linearly with offset for large automatic groups (e.g. `trust_level_0`); keyset pagination is the right shape, and no supporting index is added.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71` — `usernames.split(",")` assumes String; `params.require(:usernames)` returns an Array for `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` → `NoMethodError` 500 instead of 400. Admin-gated, so low impact; coerce with `.to_s`.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71` — N+1: one `User.find_by_username` plus one INSERT per username, no batch `User.where(username_lower: names)` and no cap on list length.

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13` — `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` instead of `Math.ceil`: one phantom page whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (50 members / limit 50 → "2").

`admin-group.js.es6:17,33` — because of the off-by-one, `showingLast` (`currentPage == totalPages`) is never true on the real last page, so Next stays enabled; `next` then clamps offset to `user_count` rather than the last page start, rendering an empty list.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23` — same `Math.min(user_count, offset)` clamp; offset is never rewound after removing the last member on a page, leaving an empty list with a stale page indicator.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-60` — neither `removeMember` nor `addMembers` has a rejection handler: a 422 (`can_not_modify_automatic`) or 500 is silently swallowed, so failed mutations show no error and the list isn't refreshed.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21` — `findMembers` now returns `undefined` for a nameless group where HEAD~2 returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`; both routes were rewritten to fire-and-forget (`admin_group_route.js:13`, `group-members.js.es6:11`), dropping `afterModel`, so members are no longer loaded before render and load errors are swallowed.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40` — the shared `Discourse.Group` model now hard-codes admin-only `/admin/groups/...` endpoints and orchestrates write-then-refetch; non-admin consumers instantiate the same class, and the orchestration belongs in the admin controller/route.

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1` — inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` the `{{#unless automatic}}` lookup resolves against the member, not the group, so the remove link is never suppressed; the UI offers an action that always 422s on automatic groups.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1` — `{{#if model}}` is now always truthy (model changed from the members array to the Group), so the empty-state guard is dead and the table header renders for zero-member groups.

`admin-group.js.es6:62` — `usernames` is never cleared after Add and never reset on route transition, so the same list can be re-posted and the field leaks across groups when switching in the admin UI.

`config/routes.rb:49` — reads are keyed by name on the public controller (`GET /groups/:name/members`) while writes are keyed by id on the admin controller (`PUT|DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members`): one sub-resource, two identifier schemes, forcing the client to hold both.

`config/routes.rb:50` — collection-append modeled as `PUT` (rather than `POST`, or `PUT /members/:user_id`), and delete targets the collection with a `user_id` param instead of `DELETE /members/:user_id`; the verbs advertise idempotency the handlers don't provide.

`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115` — `xhr :put, :remove_member` uses PUT, but the route maps only `DELETE` to `remove_member` (PUT is `add_members`). It passes only because controller specs bypass routing, so the new route wiring is never exercised.

`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:51,93,114` — automatic-group tests hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1`, relying on seed data instead of `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` as HEAD~2 did; they assert 422 without proving the group under test is automatic.

`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:49` — coverage regression: the positive rename case (`group.name.should == 'fred'`) was deleted, so renaming — the only thing `update` still does — is untested, as is `alias_level`.

`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:91` — deleted `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"`, leaving the silent-skip branch uncovered; also no coverage for blank `usernames` (`params.require` → 400), duplicates, or the error branch.
`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:112` — `.remove_member` has no coverage for a non-member/nonexistent `user_id` (currently a `RecordNotFound`) or the error branch.
`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19` — the rewritten public `members` endpoint and its new `meta` contract have no spec anywhere in this change.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:33` — drive-by removal of the `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` incremental membership API (`update_patch`) and all its specs, without deprecation, as part of an unrelated `update` rewrite.

`app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:464` — `.groups .ac-wrap { width: 100% !important; .item { margin-right: 0 !important } }` overrides the shared autocomplete wrapper (used by every user-selector) with `!important` page-wide instead of scoping to the new field; also hard-codes `#333`/`#aaa` instead of the theme color functions used elsewhere in the file.

`app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:164` — the new `.groups, .badges .form-horizontal input { width: 350px }` (0,2,1) is out-specified by the pre-existing `.row.groups input[type='text'] { width: 500px }` at line 1055 (0,3,1), so it won't apply; the stale `.row.groups` block was left untouched.
`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:28` — selector id renamed `group-users` → `user-selector`, leaving `admin_base.scss:1058` (`input#group-users`) as dead CSS.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs:5` — re-indentation of a *shared* raw handlebars template used site-wide (composer/PM/invite); as a raw template the moved newlines inject inline whitespace into the rendered anchors, which can shift autocomplete row layout for non-group features.
`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/components/admin-group-selector.hbs:1` — whitespace-only edit, pure diff noise.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:8,99`, `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:38`, `admin-group.js.es6:19`, `models/group.js:14` — cosmetic churn (`ilike`→`ILIKE`, blank lines, `protected`/`private` re-indentation, brace spacing) inflating the diff.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22` — wholesale reordering of `create`/`update`/`destroy`/`refresh_automatic_groups` (and matching spec context reshuffle) makes the real membership changes hard to review.

Overall verdict: NEEDS_REVISION.** The blocking issues are the `RecordNotFound` on non-member removal, the uncapped/unclamped public `limit`/`offset` params, the silent 50-member truncation of the public group page, and the unversioned break of the public `/groups/:name/members` response shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90` — `group.users.delete(user_id)` resolves the Integer via `find`, so removing a non-member (or stale double-click) raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` → 500 instead of the JSON contract; HEAD~2 succeeded silently and had a spec for it that this diff deleted.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90` — asymmetric lifecycle: adds go through `group.add(user)` but removals bypass `Group#remove`, deleting join rows with `delete_all` semantics — GroupUser callbacks / cached `user_count` are skipped on removal only, leaving `BasicGroupSerializer`'s `user_count` stale in the admin group list.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:77,92` — `group.save` is dead code in both `add_members` and `remove_member`: the group has no dirty attributes, so it always returns true and the `render_json_error` branch is unreachable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `add_members` and `remove_member` modifying group membership via association operations (`group.add(user)` and `group.users.delete(user_id)`). While `group.save` may often be unnecessary after such operations, it is not verifiably “dead code” from the diff: (1) `save` can still run validations/callbacks and can return `false` even if no scalar attributes changed, making the error branch theoretically reachable; and (2) we can’t confirm from the diff whether `Group#add` defers persistence until `group.save` (it was used with `group.save` previously, suggesting it may rely on it). Therefore the claim that `group.save` always returns true and the error branch is unreachable is not a strictly verifiable defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73` — re-adding an existing member is an unguarded check-then-insert: either `RecordNotUnique` (500) with a unique index, or duplicate memberships without one. Made easy to hit because the username input is never cleared.

adjudication.rationale: The new `add_members` action iterates usernames and calls `group.add(user)` without an explicit membership-exists check, but the diff does not show what `Group#add` does nor the DB constraints/validations on the membership join model. If `group.add` is already idempotent (common in Discourse) or the association handles duplicates safely, there is no bug. The claim about `RecordNotUnique`/duplicate memberships is therefore not verifiable from this diff and depends on code/schema not shown. The frontend TODO about not clearing the input is real, but it does not by itself prove the backend will error or create duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71` — no transaction around the add loop; a mid-loop failure leaves a partially applied batch and the handler is not idempotent.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, there is indeed no explicit transaction around the `usernames.split(...).each` loop. However, the proposed issue (“mid-loop failure leaves a partially applied batch” and “handler is not idempotent”) is not verifiable from this diff because it depends on how `group.add(user)` is implemented (not shown). If `group.add` only mutates in-memory state and persistence happens on the final `group.save`, then there is no partial-apply risk. Likewise, idempotency depends on whether duplicates are prevented/handled in `group.add` or via DB constraints, which is also not shown. The diff alone does not establish a concrete defect beyond a general robustness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38` — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is unconditional, so any partial PUT omitting `visible` silently makes the group invisible; every other field on the action is presence-guarded.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs unconditionally. If a client issues an update request without a `visible` parameter (e.g., only changing `alias_level` or `name`), `params[:visible]` will be `nil` and the expression evaluates to `false`, unintentionally making the group invisible. Other fields in this action are presence-guarded (`alias_level` only set if present; `name` only set if provided and not automatic), so this inconsistency is a real correctness risk visible directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:25,38` — `params[:visible] == "true"` string-compares a boolean; a JSON client sending real `true` silently gets `visible = false`.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create and #update the code sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. In Ruby, if a client submits JSON with a real boolean `true` (so `params[:visible]` is `true`), the comparison to the string "true" will be false, incorrectly forcing `visible` to false. This is directly verifiable from the diff; no coercion is performed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22` — `create` accepts only `name`/`visible`, but `Group#asJSON` always sends `alias_level`; on create it is silently dropped, requiring a second round-trip. Create and update accept divergent field sets for the same resource.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the client always includes `alias_level` in the payload via `Group#asJSON()` (see `asJSON: { name, alias_level, visible }`) and `Group#create()` POSTs that object to `/admin/groups`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` and never reads `params[:alias_level]`, so any non-default alias level chosen when creating a group is ignored (silently dropped) until a subsequent update. `Admin::GroupsController#update` *does* accept `alias_level`, so create/update have divergent accepted fields for the same resource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34` — `update` now silently *ignores* `usernames`: `PUT /admin/groups/:id` with `group[usernames]` (full member-list replace at HEAD~2) returns `success_json` while making no membership change. Silent semantics break for non-UI/API callers.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` was rewritten to read top-level params (`alias_level`, `visible`, `name`) and no longer reads `params[:group]` or applies `usernames` at all. The previous implementation explicitly handled `payload[:usernames]` to update membership via `group.usernames = ...`. Now, if a caller sends the old shape `group[usernames]=...` (or even top-level `usernames`) to `PUT /admin/groups/:id`, it will be ignored and the action can still return `success_json` because `group.save` can succeed without any changes—i.e., silent behavior change for existing API/non-UI callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22` + `admin/templates/group.hbs:12` — creating a group with an initial member set in one step is gone (member UI gated behind `{{#if id}}`); the spec covering it was deleted.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff clearly removes the ability to create/update a group while supplying initial `usernames` in the same request: the JS model drops `createWithUsernames/saveWithUsernames`, `Admin::GroupsController#create` no longer reads `params[:group][:usernames]` (it only sets `name` and `visible`), and the admin UI shows member management only under `{{#if id}}` (i.e., after the group exists). The corresponding spec that asserted creating a group with `usernames` was also removed.

However, this appears to be an intentional functional/API change paired with new separate endpoints (`add_members`/`remove_member`) and UI actions to add members after creation, not a clear defect or correctness bug introduced by mistake. Without a requirement in the diff/context that one-step creation-with-members must be supported or backward compatibility must be preserved, this is better classified as a deliberate behavior change rather than a verifiable “problem.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:52,69,88` — the `automatic` guard is hand-rolled in three actions with no `before_filter` (and `update` deliberately omits it); new actions default to unguarded, and the invariant is enforced only in the controller, not the model.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the controller explicitly guards membership-changing actions for automatic groups: `destroy` returns `can_not_modify_automatic` if `group.automatic`, and both `add_members` and `remove_member` early-return the same guard. The `update` action intentionally does *not* fully block automatic groups; it only prevents renaming (`group.name = ... if ... && !group.automatic`) while still allowing `alias_level`/`visible` updates—matching the prior behavior where automatic groups ignored rename/membership but still applied other fields. The complaint about lacking a `before_filter` and model-level enforcement is architectural/speculative rather than a verifiable bug/security defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22` — `limit` is attacker-controlled and uncapped on a publicly reachable endpoint: `GET /groups/trust_level_0/members.json?limit=99999999` serializes the entire user base — bulk enumeration + resource exhaustion. HEAD~2 had a 200 ceiling for automatic groups; this diff removed the ceiling while adding the knob. Needs `[limit, 200].min`.

`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23` — `offset = params[:offset].to_i` unvalidated → `OFFSET -1` is a Postgres `StatementInvalid` → unhandled 500. The clamp exists only client-side in `models/group.js:23`.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` from params:
```rb
offset = params[:offset].to_i
members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)
```
There is no server-side clamp/validation that `offset >= 0`. A request like `/groups/:id/members?offset=-1` will produce SQL with `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects, raising `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` and resulting in an unhandled 500. The only clamping shown in the diff is client-side in `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (`Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0)`), which does not protect the server endpoint from arbitrary requests. So this is a real robustness/correctness issue introduced/present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22` — the public endpoint now paginates *all* groups at default 50 (HEAD~2: unpaginated for non-automatic, 200 for automatic), but `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` gained no paging controls — the public group members page is silently truncated at 50 with no way to page. It also discards the HEAD~2 TODO's intent ("fix the root cause") by generalizing the truncation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit` of 50 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`), whereas previously non-automatic groups returned the full member list (no limit/offset) and only automatic groups were limited (default 200). On the client, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now calls `model.findMembers()` (which uses the model’s `limit`/`offset`) and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination UI or actions added in this diff to change `offset` for the public group members page. As a result, the public members list will show only the first page (50) by default with no built-in way to navigate to subsequent pages, making it a real functional regression/truncation introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28` — response shape changed from a bare JSON array to `{members:, meta:}`: an unversioned breaking change to a public endpoint, with no compat shim and no spec (`spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` does not exist).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (an array-style payload) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`. However, the diff also updates the in-app JS callers to expect `{members, meta}` (`group.js#findMembers`, group members route/template), so there is no demonstrated breakage within this change set. The claim that this is a “public endpoint” requiring backward compatibility and that there is “no spec” (`spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` missing) are not verifiable from the diff alone and rely on assumptions about external clients/contracts. Therefore, as stated, the finding overreaches what can be confirmed from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25` — `total = group.users.count` runs a COUNT per page fetch, duplicating the existing `user_count` column the serializer already exposes; the client overwrites the serializer value with `meta.total`, so which wins depends on load order.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new response format intentionally includes `meta.total`, so doing `total = group.users.count` is how the endpoint computes pagination metadata. This endpoint is not serializing the group itself, so it is not “duplicating the existing user_count column the serializer already exposes” in the same response. On the client, `findMembers()` deterministically sets `user_count` from `result.meta.total`, so there’s no real “which wins depends on load order” ambiguity introduced by the diff—`findMembers()` overwrites whatever was there whenever it runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26` — OFFSET pagination with `ORDER BY username_lower` over the join degrades linearly with offset for large automatic groups (e.g. `trust_level_0`); keyset pagination is the right shape, and no supporting index is added.

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint still uses LIMIT/OFFSET with ORDER BY username_lower, but that behavior for automatic groups already existed before this diff (the previous code applied limit/offset when group.automatic?). The diff mainly changes it to always paginate and to return meta/total, not introducing OFFSET pagination specifically for large automatic groups. Also, the claim that “no supporting index is added” is not verifiable from this diff (an index on users.username_lower may already exist), and the finding is largely a general performance recommendation rather than a clear defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71` — `usernames.split(",")` assumes String; `params.require(:usernames)` returns an Array for `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` → `NoMethodError` 500 instead of 400. Admin-gated, so low impact; coerce with `.to_s`.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, if the request is sent as `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` (common when a JS client passes an array), `params[:usernames]` will be an Array, which does not respond to `split`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500. The diff introduces this new endpoint and does not type-check/coerce `usernames` before calling `split`, so the robustness issue is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71` — N+1: one `User.find_by_username` plus one INSERT per username, no batch `User.where(username_lower: names)` and no cap on list length.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` action, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop performs `User.find_by_username(username)` and then `group.add(user)` for each found user. This is verifiably one DB lookup per username (and likely one membership insert per user), i.e., an N-per-item pattern rather than batching via `User.where(...)`. There is also no limit/validation on the length/size of the `usernames` string before looping, so a large input could trigger many queries/inserts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13` — `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` instead of `Math.ceil`: one phantom page whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (50 members / limit 50 → "2").
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same pagination bug: using Math.floor(...)+1 for totalPages creates an extra/phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and suggests using Math.ceil instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `admin-group.js.es6:17,33` — because of the off-by-one, `showingLast` (`currentPage == totalPages`) is never true on the real last page, so Next stays enabled; `next` then clamps offset to `user_count` rather than the last page start, rendering an empty list.
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same underlying bug: the Next action can clamp the offset to user_count/total, which makes the offset equal to the total count and produces an empty last page/list (confusing UX). The candidate adds an additional cause (off-by-one in last-page detection) but still identifies the empty-page-from-clamped-offset issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23` — same `Math.min(user_count, offset)` clamp; offset is never rewound after removing the last member on a page, leaving an empty list with a stale page indicator.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the requested offset is clamped as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), this.get("offset"))`. After `removeMember`, the code simply calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. If you remove the last member on the last page, `offset` can become equal to (or greater than) the new total, so the subsequent request uses an out-of-range offset and returns an empty `members` array. The response then sets `offset` to that out-of-range value, so UI computed `currentPage`/`totalPages` can indicate a page that has no members. This behavior is directly implied by the diff: `removeMember` does not rewind offset, and `findMembers` does not correct `offset` relative to the *new* total before querying.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-60` — neither `removeMember` nor `addMembers` has a rejection handler: a 422 (`can_not_modify_automatic`) or 500 is silently swallowed, so failed mutations show no error and the list isn't refreshed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `addMembers`/`removeMember` only attaching a success `.then(...)` and no explicit rejection handler. However, the finding’s key claim (“422 … is silently swallowed, so failed mutations show no error”) is not verifiable from this diff: error handling may be centralized in `Discourse.ajax`/global promise rejection handling (not shown here), and the UI hides these actions for automatic groups (`{{#unless automatic}}` around add/remove), so the cited 422 path is generally not reachable via the new UI. Also, not refreshing the list on failure is expected since the refresh is intentionally in the success path. As written, this is more speculative than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21` — `findMembers` now returns `undefined` for a nameless group where HEAD~2 returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`; both routes were rewritten to fire-and-forget (`admin_group_route.js:13`, `group-members.js.es6:11`), dropping `afterModel`, so members are no longer loaded before render and load errors are swallowed.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `findMembers` is now effectively fire-and-forget/async and no longer awaited (`afterModel` removed), so member data may not be loaded before rendering and errors are ignored. This is the same underlying race-condition concern as the golden comment about unhandled async `findMembers` leading to missing member data in the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40` — the shared `Discourse.Group` model now hard-codes admin-only `/admin/groups/...` endpoints and orchestrates write-then-refetch; non-admin consumers instantiate the same class, and the orchestration belongs in the admin controller/route.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `removeMember`/`addMembers` methods on the shared `Discourse.Group` model that call `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` and then refetch via `findMembers()`. However, nothing in the diff shows any non-admin route/controller invoking these write methods; they’re only wired up from the new admin UI actions in `admin-group.js.es6` and `admin/templates/group*.hbs`. Non-admin consumers (e.g., `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) only call `findMembers()`, which uses the public `/groups/:name/members.json` endpoint. So the finding is mainly an architectural preference (separation of concerns), not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1` — inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` the `{{#unless automatic}}` lookup resolves against the member, not the group, so the remove link is never suppressed; the UI offers an action that always 422s on automatic groups.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1` — `{{#if model}}` is now always truthy (model changed from the members array to the Group), so the empty-state guard is dead and the table header renders for zero-member groups.

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, `setupController` now does `controller.set("model", model);` where `model` is the Group object (`this.modelFor('group')`), and then calls `model.findMembers()` to populate a `members` property on that Group. In `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`, only the iteration was updated (`{{#each m in members}}`), but any existing guard like `{{#if model}}` at the top would now test the Group object, which is always non-empty/truthy, instead of the members array. Previously `model` was the members array, so an empty members list could make the `{{#if model}}` branch false (Ember `if` treats empty arrays as empty). This makes the empty-state conditional effectively dead and can render the table/header even when there are zero members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `admin-group.js.es6:62` — `usernames` is never cleared after Add and never reset on route transition, so the same list can be re-posted and the field leaks across groups when switching in the admin UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `usernames` is now a simple controller property (`usernames: null`) instead of the old computed property derived from `members`. The `addMembers` action posts `this.get("usernames")` to `model.addMembers(...)` and explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input`, but does not clear/reset it afterward. Additionally, `admin_group_route.js` `setupController` only sets the model and calls `model.findMembers()`; it does not reset `controller.usernames` when the route’s model changes. Since Ember route controllers are typically singletons reused across transitions, the `usernames` value can persist when switching between groups in the admin UI, leading to the same list being re-posted or appearing in the input for another group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `config/routes.rb:49` — reads are keyed by name on the public controller (`GET /groups/:name/members`) while writes are keyed by id on the admin controller (`PUT|DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members`): one sub-resource, two identifier schemes, forcing the client to hold both.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two different identifiers for group-related endpoints: reads use the public `GroupsController#members` route keyed by group name (`/groups/:group_id/members.json`, where `group_id` is the group name per `find_group(:group_id)`), while writes use admin endpoints under `/admin/groups/:id/...` (the client calls `/admin/groups/` + `this.get('id')` in `addMembers`/`removeMember`). However, this is an API design inconsistency rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff: the admin client already has both `id` and `name` on the group model (it loads the group as an admin resource and then calls `findMembers()` which uses the name; add/remove use the id). Nothing in the diff shows this causing incorrect behavior or an inability to perform operations; it’s not a verifiable bug/security/correctness issue on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `config/routes.rb:50` — collection-append modeled as `PUT` (rather than `POST`, or `PUT /members/:user_id`), and delete targets the collection with a `user_id` param instead of `DELETE /members/:user_id`; the verbs advertise idempotency the handlers don't provide.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds routes `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (under the admin group resource). While this is arguably non-RESTful (many would choose POST for “add” and `DELETE /members/:id`), it’s not a clear defect introduced by the change: both handlers behave effectively idempotently in practice (`group.add(user)` won’t duplicate membership; `group.users.delete(user_id)` is safe to repeat). Using a `user_id` parameter with `DELETE` is also a supported pattern in Rails and not inherently broken from what’s shown. So the finding is more an API design preference than a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115` — `xhr :put, :remove_member` uses PUT, but the route maps only `DELETE` to `remove_member` (PUT is `add_members`). It passes only because controller specs bypass routing, so the new route wiring is never exercised.
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same mismatch: the controller spec calls `remove_member` with `xhr :put`, while routing defines `remove_member` under a DELETE route (`delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'`). It also adds that controller specs bypass routing, but the core issue is identical.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:51,93,114` — automatic-group tests hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1`, relying on seed data instead of `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` as HEAD~2 did; they assert 422 without proving the group under test is automatic.

adjudication.rationale: The updated specs now call controller actions with hardcoded `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` for “automatic group” behavior (e.g. update context uses `xhr :put, :update, id: 1`, add_members context uses `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1`). In the diff, these tests no longer fabricate an automatic group (unlike other tests that explicitly `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`), so they implicitly rely on some pre-existing/seeded group with primary key 1 being automatic. The assertions (e.g., expecting 422) are therefore not guaranteed by the test setup and are brittle/incorrect if test data/seed order changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:49` — coverage regression: the positive rename case (`group.name.should == 'fred'`) was deleted, so renaming — the only thing `update` still does — is untested, as is `alias_level`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior update spec that asserted a normal (non-automatic) group can be renamed (`group.name.should == 'fred'`) and that update handled usernames/membership. In the controller, `update` still supports changing `name` (when not automatic), `alias_level`, and `visible`, but the updated specs only cover the negative case (automatic group ignores name change) and do not exercise a successful rename or any `alias_level` update. This is a verifiable test coverage regression in the diff (even though the finding’s phrasing that rename is the “only thing update still does” is inaccurate since `alias_level`/`visible` are also updated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:91` — deleted `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"`, leaving the silent-skip branch uncovered; also no coverage for blank `usernames` (`params.require` → 400), duplicates, or the error branch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove prior specs (including the one asserting adding a non-existent user “succeeds silently”) and the new `add_members` action indeed silently skips unknown usernames (`find_by_username` check) and will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (400) if `usernames` is absent due to `params.require(:usernames)`. However, the proposed finding is fundamentally about reduced/absent test coverage for various cases (blank input, duplicates, error branch) rather than demonstrating an actual correctness/security defect introduced by the production code in this diff. Missing coverage is not, by itself, a verifiable functional bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:112` — `.remove_member` has no coverage for a non-member/nonexistent `user_id` (currently a `RecordNotFound`) or the error branch.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is not a verifiable defect in the diff. In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` with an integer; this is generally a no-op for a non-member/nonexistent `user_id` and would not raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (no `User.find` is performed). Also, the complaint is about missing test coverage, which is not itself a functional bug introduced by the diff, and the snippet shown is truncated so the absence of additional tests cannot be conclusively verified from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19` — the rewritten public `members` endpoint and its new `meta` contract have no spec anywhere in this change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `GroupsController#members` to return a new JSON shape with a `meta` object (total/limit/offset) instead of `render_serialized(...)`. In the shown changes, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified; there is no new or updated spec covering `GroupsController#members` or validating the new `meta` contract/response structure. So the finding is grounded in the diff: a public API contract changed without accompanying test coverage in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:33` — drive-by removal of the `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` incremental membership API (`update_patch`) and all its specs, without deprecation, as part of an unrelated `update` rewrite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `update_patch` (incremental membership changes via `PATCH /admin/groups/:id`) and its associated specs, and the `update` action no longer branches on `request.patch?`. However, this is accompanied by an intentional API redesign in the same diff: new explicit membership endpoints are added (`PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` and `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`) and the JS client is updated to use `addMembers`/`removeMember` instead of patching `update`. There is no evidence in the diff of remaining in-repo callers that still depend on the old PATCH semantics, so calling it a “real defect” (as opposed to an intentional breaking change / deprecation concern) is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:464` — `.groups .ac-wrap { width: 100% !important; .item { margin-right: 0 !important } }` overrides the shared autocomplete wrapper (used by every user-selector) with `!important` page-wide instead of scoping to the new field; also hard-codes `#333`/`#aaa` instead of the theme color functions used elsewhere in the file.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new SCSS block scoped under `.groups { ... }`, so `.groups .ac-wrap { width: 100% !important; ... }` only applies within elements inside a `.groups` container, not “page-wide” across every user-selector/autocomplete wrapper. The admin group template also adds its own `div.ac-wrap` for the member list, so the styling appears intentionally targeted to the groups area. The complaint about hard-coded `#333/#aaa` vs theme color helpers is a theming/style preference, not a verifiable correctness/bug issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:164` — the new `.groups, .badges .form-horizontal input { width: 350px }` (0,2,1) is out-specified by the pre-existing `.row.groups input[type='text'] { width: 500px }` at line 1055 (0,3,1), so it won't apply; the stale `.row.groups` block was left untouched.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a Sass block `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { input, textarea, select { width: 350px; } ... } }`, which compiles to selectors like `.groups .form-horizontal input` and `.badges .form-horizontal input` (not `.groups, .badges .form-horizontal input` as the finding states). The alleged overriding rule `.row.groups input[type='text'] { width: 500px }` is not shown anywhere in the provided diff, so the claimed specificity conflict cannot be verified from this change. Without evidence that such a `.row.groups` rule exists and applies to this form, the finding is speculative/misreads the selector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:28` — selector id renamed `group-users` → `user-selector`, leaving `admin_base.scss:1058` (`input#group-users`) as dead CSS.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the `user-selector` element’s `id` changing from `group-users` (old template) to `user-selector` (new template). However, the claim that `admin_base.scss:1058` still contains `input#group-users` (and is therefore dead CSS) is not verifiable from this diff because that selector is not shown anywhere in the provided `admin_base.scss` changes. Without the referenced CSS line appearing in the diff, we can’t confirm the dead/unused CSS problem based solely on the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs:5` — re-indentation of a *shared* raw handlebars template used site-wide (composer/PM/invite); as a raw template the moved newlines inject inline whitespace into the rendered anchors, which can shift autocomplete row layout for non-group features.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` only changes indentation and moves the closing `` onto its own line. In normal HTML rendering, the added newline/indentation becomes collapsible whitespace and does not reliably inject visible spacing that would “shift autocomplete row layout” unless CSS is explicitly preserving whitespace (e.g., `white-space: pre`), which is not shown in the diff. This is therefore not a verifiable functional defect introduced by the change based on the provided patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/components/admin-group-selector.hbs:1` — whitespace-only edit, pure diff noise.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/components/admin-group-selector.hbs`, the diff only removes blank lines around the existing `<input type="text">` line. This is a whitespace-only change that does not alter behavior, introduce a bug, or create a correctness/security defect. It may be considered minor diff noise, but that is not a verifiable functional problem per the criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:8,99`, `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:38`, `admin-group.js.es6:19`, `models/group.js:14` — cosmetic churn (`ilike`→`ILIKE`, blank lines, `protected`/`private` re-indentation, brace spacing) inflating the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The cited changes (e.g., `ilike`→`ILIKE`, added/removed blank lines, indentation of `protected`/`private` helper methods, and brace/spacing tweaks) are cosmetic refactors that do inflate the diff, but they do not introduce a verifiable bug, security issue, or functional defect in the shown code. This is a style/readability nit rather than a correctness problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22` — wholesale reordering of `create`/`update`/`destroy`/`refresh_automatic_groups` (and matching spec context reshuffle) makes the real membership changes hard to review.

adjudication.rationale: The cited issue is about code organization/reordering (“makes membership changes hard to review”), which is a subjective reviewability/style concern rather than a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness problem) introduced by the diff. The diff does reorder controller methods and spec contexts, but that does not constitute a functional problem in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Overall verdict: NEEDS_REVISION.** The blocking issues are the `RecordNotFound` on non-member removal, the uncapped/unclamped public `limit`/`offset` params, the silent 50-member truncation of the public group page, and the unversioned break of the public `/groups/:name/members` response shape.
